problem: Which of the following functions is continuous on the interval $(-\infty ,2]?$  You may assume that all points of discontinuity for each function are shown.
worked_solution:
The correct answer is the following.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945275/assets/7afb04e0197b44ffadeee53bc365910f7c578eb8a3f2e2971a83f4f51947a3af.png)

We see that $q(x)$ is continuous on the interval $(-\infty ,3],$ and since $(-\infty ,2]$ lies completely inside $(-\infty ,3],$ it is also continuous on $(-\infty ,2].$

Notice that

- $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are not continuous at $x=-1$, and so are not continuous on $(-\infty ,2].$

- $p(x)$ and $h(x)$ are not continuous at $x=0$, and so are not continuous on $(-\infty ,2].$
